title: Surge Jettison Controller and Model Graceful-Degrade Orchestration
creator: Priya Singh
description: Implement a runtime-level 'Surge Jettison Controller' that synthesizes per-dependency, per-model, and per-tenant trip signals and orchestrates safe degraded paths. Goal is to reduce blast radius during spikes and region failovers while preserving correctness and observability. The controller must support soft-attenuation (stepped shedding), deterministic hard-open policies, canary reopen probes, and safe fallback routing to compatible model variants, cached prefixes, or feature-degraded responses.
acceptance_criteria: Controller computes trip state for dependency/model/tenant independently and emits events (closed, soft-open, hard-open, probe).
Soft-open path reduces traffic to a dependency by configurable percent steps (default: 10%, 25%, 50%) and honors tenant tiers.
Hard-open routes requests away from affected dependency to a predefined fallback set (quantized model, cached reply, or simpler model) with zero data exfiltration.
Canary probes automatically resume traffic in controlled increments after stabilization windows and surface diagnostics in Console rollouts.
All state transitions, thresholds, and per-tenant overrides are visible in Console and recorded in trace logs and SLO dashboards.
implementation_steps: 1) Design: finalize signal set and state machine (Closed / SoftOpen / HardOpen / Probe).
2) Metrics: add sliding-window counters for errors, p50/p95/p99 latency, queue depth, and backend saturation score. Use 1m and 5m windows with EWMA smoothing.

3) Thresholds: implement baseline-aware thresholds (baseline derived from 7d historical percentiles per tenant/model). Soft-trip when (error_rate > 3% OR p99 > 3x baseline) for 1m; hard-trip when conditions persist for 5m.
4) Traffic shaping: implement attenuation token that probabilistically drops or reroutes X% of traffic; support deterministic hashing for session-affinity.
5) Fallbacks: wire routing table to prefer fallback models (configured per model family) or cached prefixes. Ensure fallback models are vetted and have separate capacity pools.
6) Console: build UI for per-tenant overrides, manual trip, and live metrics. Add API to temporarily whitelist tenants.
7) Tracing/logging: emit structured events for state transitions, reason codes, and affected keys (tenant/model/dependency).
8) Testing: unit tests for state machine; integration tests using chaos harness (latency injection, error injection); load tests exercising stepped attenuation.
9) Rollout: feature flag behind runtime-2.4 gate with canary in two non-prod regions, then gradual ramp to staging and prod.
monitoring_and_alerting: SLOs: new derived SLO dashboard showing availability and latency per tenant and per model-family (objective: 99.5% p95 availability).
Alerts: firing when >5 tenants hit SoftOpen simultaneously OR any tenant enters HardOpen for >2m.
Runbook link: internal runbook for Surge Jettison (playbook id: RJ-12).
Dashboards: runtime/surge-jettison (grafana id: dg-879), console shows transition events in last 24h.
rollout_plan: Phase 0: Library-level merge behind feature flag (code review and unit tests).
Phase 1: Canary in region-us-west-2 with 5 low-impact test tenants. Monitor for false positives for 48h.
Phase 2: Expand to staging, run synthetic traffic + chaos (latency spikes + dependency failures).
Phase 3: Gradual prod ramp—enable for 10% of traffic, then 50%, then 100% over 7 days with rollback policy.
test_plan: Unit tests: state machine invariants and hysteresis behavior.
Integration: simulate model GPU OOM and backend error surge; assert traffic is rerouted to configured fallback with latency < fallback-sla.
Load test: sustained 10x baseline QPS for 15 minutes observing stepped attenuation and no customer-visible 500s beyond accepted budget.
Chaos: region outage simulation to validate multi-region failover respects per-tenant capacity and does not cascade into unrelated regions.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: false-positive trips for short-lived transient spikes. Mitigation: EWMA smoothing + dual-window confirmation (1m + 5m) and conservative defaults.
Risk: fallback model quality regression. Mitigation: require explicit fallback approval for each model family and pre-rollout QA.
Risk: per-tenant quota starvation when many tenants fall back to shared smaller model. Mitigation: per-tenant throttles + reserved capacity for critical customers.
Risk: operator confusion. Mitigation: Console UX improvements and explicit state explanations and links to runbook in alerts.
